back: Session hosts make outbound connections only — no inbound port, no public IP on a host. Keyword: never open inbound RDP.
Keep round-trip time below roughly 150 ms; it is what drives region choice. Keyword: RTT decides the region.
Direct UDP path between client and host instead of relaying through the gateway. Managed-network and public-network flavours. Keyword: skip the gateway.
DSCP marking prioritises the UDP stream, which only exists once Shortpath is carrying the session. Keyword: order matters.
Gives the feed and gateway private endpoints so connections never traverse the public internet. Keyword: private control plane.
SMB on SSD with IOPS provisioned by share size and identity-based auth. The usual profile answer. Keyword: premium, not standard.
For larger scale or sub-millisecond latency and very high IOPS, at higher cost. Keyword: extreme performance.

front: Two permission levels on a profile share
back: Share-level Azure RBAC for SMB access plus NTFS permissions inside. Missing either gives a temporary profile. Keyword: both layers.
Pooled shares multi-session hosts between users. Personal assigns one host per user permanently. Keyword: shared vs dedicated.
Breadth-first spreads sessions for best performance. Depth-first fills a host first for best density and lower cost. Keyword: experience vs cost.
Windows Enterprise multi-session is for pooled pools only; personal pools need single-session Windows. Keyword: pooled means multi-session.
Groups application groups into the user's feed. An unregistered application group is invisible however it is assigned. Keyword: no workspace, no feed.
Application groups — never to host pools. Keyword: application group.
Time-limited; an expired token is the usual reason a newly built host never joins the pool. Keyword: regenerate it.
Generalise before capturing an image, or hosts collide on identity and fail to register. Keyword: generalise.
Versions replicate across regions with replica counts, so a large or multi-region rollout does not throttle. Keyword: replicas.
Need RDS Client Access Licences from a reachable licence server — unlike Windows Enterprise multi-session. Keyword: RDS CALs.
Opts a host pool into service updates early so changes are tested before reaching production pools. Keyword: canary pool.
A user must exist in the directory the session host trusts; a cloud-only user cannot sign in to an AD DS-joined host. Keyword: both sides must agree.
What lets Entra-joined session hosts authenticate to an Azure Files profile share. Keyword: Entra join plus Azure Files.
Configured on the host pool with a Kerberos server object; removes the second credential prompt at connection. Keyword: two prompts means no SSO.
Application group assignment lets a user connect. Administering objects needs a Desktop Virtualization role. Keyword: separate planes.
The role that permits signing in to an Entra-joined session host — separate from application group assignment. Keyword: sign-in right.
Azure Virtual Desktop covers the connection; Microsoft Remote Desktop covers the client feed. Keyword: target both.
Exclude container files from Defender Antivirus or profile attach is slow and sometimes fails. Keyword: configuration, not tuning.

front: Onboard Defender for Endpoint in the image
back: So every host built from it is onboarded automatically instead of individually afterwards. Keyword: bake it in.
Azure Bastion, or just-in-time VM access — not RDP from the internet. Keyword: no public management port.
Trusted launch gives secure boot and vTPM for boot integrity. A confidential VM encrypts memory against the host. Keyword: boot vs memory.
A VHDX holding the whole user profile, attached at sign-in so it appears local on whichever host the user lands on. Keyword: roaming solved.
Holds Office data — Outlook cache, OneNote, licensing — separately from the profile container. Keyword: Office split out.
Writes the container to more than one storage provider and fails over. The resilience answer, at a performance cost. Keyword: survive an outage.
Hides apps, fonts, and registry entries from users who should not see them, so one image serves several populations. Keyword: one image, many entitlements.
The answer when nothing may be installed on the endpoint. Keyword: no install.

front: RDP properties on the host pool
back: Where redirection, display, and connection behaviour are set for everyone using the pool. Keyword: pool-wide switchboard.
Offloads video playback and calls to the local client instead of rendering on the host. Keyword: don't render on the server.
Removes print servers entirely — the cloud-only printing answer. Keyword: no print server.
Deallocates hosts and starts one when a user connects, trading a start-up delay for compute cost. Keyword: pay only when used.
Mounts an application package at sign-in so it is delivered without being installed. Update by publishing a new package. Keyword: no image rebuild.
Publishes individual applications rather than a full desktop. Keyword: just the app.
Required for Microsoft 365 Apps on multi-session hosts; without it activation fails. Keyword: multi-session needs SCA.
Required for Teams so audio and video are handled by the local client rather than the session host. Keyword: offload the call.
Diagnostic settings on host pool, workspace, and application groups plus host counters and events into Log Analytics. Keyword: empty Insights means missing config.
Round-trip time and bandwidth — where a responsiveness complaint is confirmed or dismissed. Keyword: is it the network.
The performance signal that points at storage rather than at CPU when sign-in is slow. Keyword: slow sign-in.
Ramp-up, peak, ramp-down, off-peak — each with an algorithm and a capacity threshold. Keyword: four phases.
Notification message, delay, and whether to force sign-out — how users are treated while a host drains. Keyword: draining politely.
Stops new sessions reaching a host while existing ones continue — maintenance without disconnecting anybody. Keyword: quiesce.
Patch the image, publish a version, rebuild hosts. Pooled hosts are disposable. Keyword: replace, don't patch.
They carry the user's installed state, so they are patched in place with Update Manager or Intune. Keyword: cannot be rebuilt.
Profile containers on Azure Files and personal desktops. Pooled session hosts are rebuilt from an image, not backed up. Keyword: back up the irreplaceable.
